verifications.claim: NASA launched the Artemis II mission on April 1, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'The Artemis II crew blasted off ... on Wednesday' (URL: 2026/04/01); R5: 'NASA’s Artemis II mission has officially lifted off at 6:35 p.m. EDT'; R6: 'lifted off ... at 6:35 p.m. ET'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly confirm the launch occurred on April 1, 2026, at approximately 6:35 p.m. ET.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission sent four astronauts on a 10-day,8-hour journey around the Moon and back.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: R1: 'four astronauts ... 10-day mission ... around the moon but not land there ... splashdown ... on April 10'; R2: 'Four astronauts ... 10 days'; R3: 'four astronauts on a 10-day voyage around the moon'
verifications.reasoning: Sources consistently describe a 10-day mission with four astronauts around the moon and back, but none specify '8-hour'; duration is broadly supported as ~10 days (e.g., April 1 to 10), making it less precise.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission is the first crewed lunar flight since 1972.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'The last time astronauts traveled that far was Apollo 17, in December 1972'; R4: 'first crewed moon mission since 1972'; R2: 'first time astronauts return to the vicinity of the moon in more than 50 years'
verifications.reasoning: Sources directly state it is the first crewed lunar mission since Apollo 17 in 1972.
